evals.prompt: research deeply whether we should move immich off rootless podman, the networking keeps fighting us
evals.expected_output: Deep track first turn: grounds in the full Immich configs and the incident record, notes there is no documented networking problem, asks for the concrete symptom before any conclusion or hypothesis, keeps any likely backlog additions short, and does no outside research.
expectations: Reads the full Immich container or service config files (not only design docs) before responding
Checks incident documentation (docs/05_incidents/) or BACKLOG.md for a record of the networking problem
The final message tells the operator whether a documented record of the problem was found and asks for the concrete symptom
No verdict, recommendation, diagnosis, or hypothesis about the cause appears before the questions in the final message
Any 'Likely backlog additions' section has at most five items, one line each
No web or MCP research is performed before the operator check-in
The response does not announce or justify the research track

evals.prompt: research lightly what zigbee coordinator people are running with home assistant these days
evals.expected_output: Light track answered in one turn: grounded in the Zigbee2MQTT config, opens with stated assumptions, presents several options with confidence-tagged and dated primary-leaning sources related to the current setup, offers at most a labeled lean, lists the plaintext network_key under Likely backlog additions, and lists local references. No stop to ask questions first and no probing of why the question was asked.
expectations: Reads the Zigbee2MQTT config in the homelab repo before answering
Answers in this turn instead of stopping to ask questions before researching
The answer opens with explicitly stated assumptions the operator can correct
The answer never asks what prompted the question or why the operator is asking
Presents more than one option, and every claim carries exactly one of confirmed, likely, or speculative
Every claim tagged confirmed traces to a page fetch or file read in actions.md, not only a search result
Cites a URL and date for each claim, with at least one vendor or project primary source per option
Relates the options to the current setup found in the repo (existing adapter and Zigbee2MQTT)
Offers at most a lean explicitly labeled as a lean, not a decision
Lists the plaintext network_key under a 'Likely backlog additions' section and asks whether to add it to the backlog, without fixing it
Includes a Local references list of repo paths near the end, before only the closing question
The response does not announce or justify the research track

evals.prompt: research dispatcharr vs threadfin for our iptv flow
evals.expected_output: Grounds in the existing iptv research and service configs, stops to ask the operator to clone both repos to ~/repos before researching their source, lists likely backlog additions with a backlog question, and names no winner.
expectations: The response does not announce or justify the research track
Reads the existing research/iptv_flow_dispatcharr.md before responding
The final message states what the config/services/ check found for Dispatcharr and Threadfin (present, absent, or partial)
Checks ~/repos for existing clones, then stops to ask the operator to clone any missing dispatcharr or threadfin repositories before researching their source
Does not fetch repository source files piece by piece over the web or API
The final message has a 'Likely backlog additions' section with at least one item (undeclared Dispatcharr deployment, broken doc link, or similar) and asks whether to add them to the backlog
